business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Ultra-HD 4K Minimally Invasive Rigid Endoscopes

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of the Marshall Islands — Non-Resident Business Corporation (BC) regime, Majuro Registry
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — unitary national corporate law modeled on United States common law statutes (the Business Corporations Act 1990 is derived from the Delaware General Corporation Law and the Model Business Corporation Act), with customary land-law matters separate and inapplicable to this non-resident entity; no sub-state tax or regulatory distinction.

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States, as amended, 2003 — Treaty of Amity and Economic Relations providing MFN economic and trade relations.
Pacific Islands Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA), 2001 — intra-Pacific trade-in-goods liberalization framework.

No comprehensive double tax agreement (DTAA) network is in force; non-resident BC profits are administered on an exempt basis, and reliance is placed on the RMI tax-exempt regime rather than treaty protection.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, as amended, Republic of the Marshall Islands (administered by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit, FIU); Business Corporations Act 1990 (Title 51, Chapter 4, RMI Revised Code, as amended), including the confidential Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) obligation implemented under the RMI's FATF/APG reform program; Foreign Investment Business License Act 2001 (FIBLA); supporting FIU Guidance Notes on CDD, PEPs, and record-keeping, and relevant Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) standards.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the RMI Beneficial Ownership Register is confidential and is not a public register; access is limited to the Registrar of Corporations, the RMI FIU, and foreign competent authorities acting through authorized mutual legal assistance channels.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passport and proof of residential address for each director, shareholder, and 25%+ beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of residence, jointly attested by the RMI-licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the origin country is an Apostille contracting state) OR consular legalization through the RMI Permanent Mission to the United Nations / nearest RMI honorary consulate for non-Apostille states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and current constitutional documents of any corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State, Hong Kong Companies Registry, PRC SAMR, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization depending on the registry jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter covering the shareholder's and UBO's banking relationship, account conduct, and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution, signed by an authorized branch officer and attested by a notary public in the institution's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn statement of source of wealth / source of funds for the initial capitalization contribution supporting the Swift_LC and TT_Wire payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or certified public accountant in the capital provider's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (POA) authorizing the RMI registered agent to reserve the company name, execute the Articles of Incorporation, and file UBO returns
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's jurisdiction, countersigned by the RMI-licensed registered agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of each director, shareholder, and 25%+ UBO against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, US OFAC SDN list, UK HMT sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, RMI sanctions notices implementing UNSCR obligations, World Bank/ADB debarment lists, and Interpol notices. Automatic enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered by any PEP or adverse-media match, requiring documented source of wealth, senior-management sign-off prior to incorporation, and enhanced scrutiny before activation of SWIFT letters of credit (MT700) and T/T wire (MT103) payment channels. FIU-regulated agents must maintain CDD records for at least five years and file suspicious transaction reports (STR) within the statutory threshold where material inconsistencies appear.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro), administered under the Attorney-General's docket; formal name availability search is effected exclusively through an RMI-licensed registered agent because no unrestricted public database exists, and the Registrar conducts a written lexical-similarity review against the active BC and LLC registers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must appear in Latin (Roman) script; English and Marshallese are equally acceptable, and any foreign-script trading name requires a mandatory English transliteration in the Articles of Incorporation. The name must be distinguishable on the register, must not be obscene or imply a misleading governmental, professional, or charitable connection, and must close with Corporation, Incorporated, Limited, or abbreviations Corp., Inc., or Ltd.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant through the registered agent may, within 30 days, file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations attaching registry evidence of prior use, consent documents for sensitive tokens, or a refined distinguishing element. The Registrar must issue a written determination; if the refusal is affirmed, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of the Marshall Islands within 30 days of that determination. In parallel, a substitute name should be reserved immediately to avoid transactional delay. The statutory 120-day reservation is not extendable, but a fresh reservation application may be filed on expiry without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible — the RMI Business Corporation may be entirely non-resident with no physical operating premises in the Marshall Islands. The statutory registered office is the physical street address of the licensed registered agent in Majuro, utilized solely for service of process and official filings. For this medical-device manufacturer, which will conduct actual production and sales outside the RMI, a virtual office structure satisfies the statutory mandate.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk — approximately 5–10% probability of a government-initiated unannounced physical inspection of the registered office for a standard-risk, non-resident manufacturing entity; the Registrar and FIU rely on desk-based risk screening and targeted examinations rather than factory site visits, with on-site scrutiny escalating only upon a suspicious transaction report or regulatory investigation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Title 59 (Corporations), Sections 31 through 58 and 70 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Business Corporation. The company may commence business with zero issued shares; if capital is paid, it must be deposited in a domestic bank account maintained in compliance with BCA Section 44.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers executing the Articles of Incorporation are designated incorporators and the form of Articles previously circulated is approved; that the registered office shall be established at the address of the Registered Agent at Trust Company Complex, Majuro, Marshall Islands; that the following directors are elected to the initial board: [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C]; that the officers shall be a President, Secretary, and Treasurer as set forth in the officer list; and that the President is authorized to open bank accounts, execute financing instruments, appoint professional advisors, and complete all filings necessary for incorporation and the initial licensing process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Assessment and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation inquiry through an accredited Registered Agent or directly to the Business Entities Division. Verify that the desired corporate name is distinguishable from all existing names in RMI records and that the proposed Registered Agent has consented to serve as the statutory agent for the corporation.
required_dossiers: Written Consent of the Proposed Registered Agent (Form RA-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a formal name reconsideration request with the Registrar providing justification; alternatively, select an available variation and refile within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed in the Marshall Islands or a foreign notary with apostille certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation in accordance with BCA Section 31, including corporate name, registered agent, registered office, purpose statement, authorized share structure, and incorporator details. Attach the initial Bylaws and obtain notarized signatures of all incorporators. Ensure that the apostille certification is affixed if the notary acts outside the Republic.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (original and three copies)
Statement of Registration of Registered Agent (Form RA-2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarization is defective for lack of an apostille, cure by having a consular officer of the Republic of the Marshall Islands authenticate the signatures, then resubmit within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the notarized Articles of Incorporation and required forms to the Registrar, together with the official filing fee of USD 300. Payment may be made by wire transfer to the RMI Attorney General's account or through the online filing portal operated by the Business Entities Division. The Registrar shall issue an acknowledgment of filing containing the date and time of receipt.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation with original signatures
Statement of Registration of Registered Agent (Form RA-2)
Proof of Wire Transfer or Filing Fee Voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query letter or deficiency notice, submit a written explanatory response addressing each item within 10 business days. If the 10-day period is missed, the application is deemed abandoned; refile with a new date and pay a reinstatement fee of 50% of the original filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Entities Division, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar will endorse the Articles and issue a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the official seal. The company may also obtain a corporate seal, minute book, and blank share certificates from the Registered Agent or an approved corporate supplies vendor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is lost or contains a typographical error, apply to the Registrar for a replacement certified copy under BCA Section 45; the Registrar will reissue upon submission of a notarized indemnity and correction fee of USD 25.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Appointments, and Registered Office Record Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation and the Office of the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors (or obtain unanimous written consent under BCA Section 36(c)). Adopt the initial board resolution, authorize the issuance of shares to incorporators, elect officers, and approve the registered office address as the principal administrative seat. Record the minutes in the corporate minute book and retain copies at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Written Consent in Lieu of First Board Meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the written consent is later found to be procedurally defective, the board may adopt a corrective resolution nunc pro tunc under BCA Section 37, confirming all prior actions as of their original effective dates.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Human Services, Medical Device Manufacturing Licensing Division, Republic of the Marshall Islands
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Establishment License (Class II – Sterile Manufacturing of Rigid Endoscopes)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A – Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report (due to continuous industrial operations, wastewater discharge, and solvent use in metal finishing and optical assembly)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent must meet RMI EPA National Effluent Standards: pH 6.5–8.5, biological oxygen demand (BOD) < 50 mg/L, total suspended solids < 50 mg/L, heavy metals (e.g. chromium, nickel) below 0.1 mg/L. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from solvent-based cleaning must not exceed 0.5 kg/hour per exhaust stack. Hazardous waste (argon, lubricants, etchant residues) must be contained, stored, and disposed at a licensed waste facility with manifest documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Civil Defense Certification issued by the RMI Fire Safety Inspection Bureau covering emergency egress, fire suppression systems, and electrical load safety. Structural load inspection must be conducted by a registered civil engineer to confirm the floor capacity of the manufacturing cleanroom and storage mezzanine. Occupational Safety and Health Clearance from the RMI Occupational Safety and Health Section covering machine guarding, chemical hygiene plan, and personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance for cleanroom personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Tax Administration (RTA), Ministry of Finance, Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI). Principal office: Delap, Majuro, with an Ebeye branch; TIN issuance, income tax, gross revenue tax, and customs/export clearance are consolidated within the RTA. Official portal: the RTA 'Tax Services' gateway on the RMI Ministry of Finance web portal; no fully automated self-service TIN/VAT portal is available for non-resident exempt entities, which file through registered agents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the Business Corporation (BC) under the Business Corporations Act 1990 through an RMI-licensed registered agent; the RMI Registrar of Corporations issues the Certificate of Incorporation, whose registration number becomes the entity's master identifier. Step 2 - If the BC carries on physical business in the RMI, file the admission/registration with the Registrar of Foreign Corporations and obtain a Business License under the Business License Act 2005 (fee scales tied to gross revenue bands). Step 3 - Apply to the RTA for a 9-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) on the entity registration form if the BC derives RMI-source income, employs staff in the RMI, or needs a customs/tax account for goods movements. Step 4 - No VAT or GST ID exists to procure because no VAT/GST system has been enacted; the Certificate of Incorporation and, where applicable, the Business License serve as operative tax identity for banking and export purposes. Step 5 - Complete RTA Customs exporter/consignor registration at the port of export to obtain the exporter code referenced on each Customs Export Declaration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box classification election exists in RMI law. Available statutory election and status mechanisms: (1) Non-Resident Designation - the articles of incorporation may declare the BC to be a non-resident corporation, automatically limiting tax exposure to RMI-source activity under the Income Tax Act 1989; (2) Exempt International Entity Election - a certified application to the RTA/Ministry of Finance for statutory tax-exempt status for qualifying international entities (e.g., international shipping under the RMI Maritime Act and international banking under the International Banking Act); (3) Entity-Form Election - promoters may choose to constitute the vehicle as a BC, LLC, limited partnership, or limited duration company, each producing a different foreign tax classification profile; (4) Hybrid Mismatch - the RMI has not enacted the OECD BEPS Action 2 domestic hybrid mismatch rules, so no hybrid instrument, hybrid entity, or branch mismatch elections are available; taxpayers relying on foreign entity classification must self-assess under the general territorial sourcing rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Hybrid indirect tax regime without VAT/GST: (i) Customs Import Duty under the RMI Tariff Act and Customs Regulations (ad valorem tariff schedule) and (ii) Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) under the Gross Revenue Tax Act 1989 at 3% of RMI-source gross revenue. Export sales of manufactured goods to non-resident buyers are excluded from gross revenue and are de facto zero-rated; no VAT input-credit or refund chain exists, and import-duty relief on inputs incorporated into exported goods is handled through customs inward-processing/duty-remission rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Official currency: United States dollar (USD), the legal currency of the RMI. GRT and Business License registration: a business carrying on RMI-source activity must register once projected or actual annual gross revenue reaches the de minimis threshold of USD 10,000; below that level a token license/filing obligation applies. A non-resident BC with zero RMI-source revenue is beneath any threshold. No VAT registration threshold exists because no VAT/GST law has been enacted.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance mandate applies: no e-invoicing standard, no SAF-T/PEPPOL/XML invoicing format, no digital tax stamping, and no clearance API or fiscal-device certification regime governs commercial invoices. Taxpayers must issue serially numbered invoices and retain books and records for the statutory retention period. For physical exports, the RTA Customs Division requires an electronic Customs Export Declaration transmitted through its internal customs clearance platform; that filing is a trade-control document and is not a substitute for fiscal invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility criteria for de facto zero-rating of exports: (1) the goods (ultra-HD 4K minimally invasive rigid endoscopes and laparoscopy tower components manufactured under ISIC 3250) must be sold under a contract with a buyer located outside the RMI, with title and risk passing outside RMI territory; (2) the sale proceeds must be received in USD or another foreign currency from non-resident sources, with no RMI-source revenue element; (3) if components are imported into the RMI and re-exported after incorporation into finished towers, the importer must claim inward-processing/duty-remission treatment at importation and maintain a factory movement record; (4) services performed in the RMI for non-resident customers qualify for GRT exclusion only where the benefit is entirely realized offshore; (5) the BC must maintain its non-resident status declaration and, if audited, evidence the absence of an RMI permanent establishment through board-meeting and management-location records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (RMI Customs export form referencing the exporter/consignor registration code)
Commercial Invoice and detailed Packing List (serially numbered and consistent with physical inventory records)
Bill of Lading or House/Neutral Air Waybill evidencing offshore destination and transfer of title
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT payment advice confirming receipt of the export proceeds within the repatriation deadline
Certified Certificate of Incorporation and non-resident status declaration (with Business License and GRT exclusion endorsement, if held)
Certificate of Origin or customs inward-processing/duty-remission paperwork where free-zone or re-export relief is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RTA may reopen export claims for the statutory limitation period (7 years; unlimited where fraud is established). If a claimed export sale is reclassified as RMI-source revenue, the RTA retroactively assesses the 3% GRT on the gross invoice value, adds statutory interest at the published monthly rate, and imposes a civil penalty of up to 50% of the understated tax. Participation in false or fraudulent documentation triggers criminal prosecution under the Income Tax Act 1989 (fine and/or imprisonment up to 5 years) and customs offences involving seizure, forfeiture, and administrative fines up to the full value of the goods or the duty evaded, whichever is greater. Registered agents and corporate officers who knowingly certify false zero-rating or export documents face personal liability and license revocation, and the taxpayer may be required to post a customs bond before further exports are cleared.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI). The official legal tender is the United States dollar; monetary policy and currency convertibility conditions are therefore governed by the U.S. Federal Reserve as issuer of the circulating currency. Banking licensing and prudential supervision are exercised by the Banking Commissioner, Ministry of Finance, under the Banking Act 1991; AML/CFT supervision is supported by the Financial Intelligence Unit attached to the Office of the Attorney General.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender, and the RMI maintains no foreign-exchange control legislation. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible and unrestricted: there are no statutory restrictions on the remittance of dividends, interest, loan repayments, or proceeds from capital reduction or liquidation. A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) not engaged in trade or business within the RMI is exempt from income tax and gross revenue tax, and the RMI imposes no dividend withholding tax; consequently, the only practical remittance hurdle is the correspondent bank's own sanctions screening and AML due diligence, not RMI statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. The RMI imposes no statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds. Receivables may be retained in USD or any permitted foreign currency at the BC's discretion, either onshore in an RMI-licensed bank or offshore. The entity should, however, maintain a complete trade documentation file (commercial invoices, bills of lading, Letter of Credit or MT103 records) to satisfy the bank's ongoing transaction monitoring and to support the tax-exempt non-resident status.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account; separate USD Capital Escrow Account for initial share-subscription proceeds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam - Marshall Islands Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account; Trade Finance Account for documentary Letters of Credit and standby Letters of Credit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. The RMI has no electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime under the Banking Act 1991, and non-resident business corporations are not statutorily barred from holding accounts with foreign fintech banks. In practice, however, reputable EU/UK/Asia-Pacific EMIs classify RMI tax-exempt BCs as offshore or shell-risk profiles and commonly decline onboarding because of downstream U.S. correspondent-bank de-risking. Where available, fintech accounts are non-credit, payment-only wallets with stringent transaction limits and no documentary trade-finance capability. Legal constraint: any foreign EMI must be fully authorized in its home jurisdiction, and the RMI entity must still deliver beneficial-ownership declarations, source-of-funds evidence, and board resolutions to the EMI's compliance function.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statute under the Banking Act 1991 or the RMI AML/CFT Act 2020 mandates an in-person director appearance before an RMI-licensed bank. Remote account opening is permissible if the bank completes enhanced customer due diligence: apostilled or notarized certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, registered-agent confirmation, board resolution appointing signatories, UBO declarations, and a live video-verification interview of directors and signatories. In bank practice, at least one senior officer may be required to attend an in-person interview at the branch or to undergo a notarized video interview, sometimes supported by a 'comfort letter' from a qualifying overseas bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident, tax-exempt BC with no physical operations in the RMI and no audited financial history (shell-risk flag in the bank's CDD engine).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; registered agent and registered office confirmation; board resolution authorizing account opening; group ownership chart and UBO declaration (name, date of birth, nationality, residency, source of funds); detailed business plan for the 4K laparoscopy-tower manufacturing and distribution business; executed master supply and distribution agreements; first-year cash-flow forecast; written commitment to provide audited financial statements within 12 months of the accounting year-end.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO, director, or signatory resident in, or funds originating from, an FATF grey-listed, EU high-risk third-country, or OFAC/UN sanctions-restricted jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO identification package (passport, proof of address, tax identification number); source-of-wealth narrative with supporting records (salary, share-sale agreements, dividend statements); completed PEP and sanctions screening clearance; signed enhanced due diligence questionnaire; professional reference letter from the UBO's existing banker or licensed attorney; destination-of-funds undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-device manufacturing classification (ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339112) without visible product or export regulatory licenses, triggering trade-compliance and product-safety scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory license or registration held by the manufacturing operation: ISO 13485:2016 quality-management-system certificate; EU CE marking certificate under Medical Device Regulation 2017/745 or U.S. FDA establishment registration and device listing; product technical file and instructions for use; RMI business license (where applicable); end-user certificates and distributor agreements for target markets; IEC 60601-series electrical safety and EMC test reports; sterilization validation where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-velocity USD inflows and outflows (capital injection followed by trade payments to Asian and EU suppliers) without a demonstrable trade cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales contract or frame purchase agreement with hospital-distributor customers; purchase orders and pro-forma invoices for raw materials and optical/electronic components of the laparoscopy towers; proposed clearing profile (expected transaction volumes, counterparties, and jurisdictions); letter of indemnity and corporate guarantee; executed documentary Letter of Credit template (UCP 600) evidencing the trade-finance loop.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funds must be remitted as USD wire transfers using SWIFT MT103 message format, cleared over Fedwire or CHIPS through the beneficiary bank's U.S. correspondent. The payment message must identify the remitter, the beneficiary BC, the account number, and a clear purpose memo, e.g., 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - SUBSCRIPTION FOR SHARES' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - PROJECT MARSHALL'. The RMI imposes no exchange-control filing, but the receiving bank will require the full account-opening dossier, a board resolution approving the capital injection, and issuance records for the corresponding shares or debt instruments; large-value wires may trigger suspicious-transaction reporting under the RMI AML/CFT Act 2020 and should be supported by a source-of-funds letter.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for endoscope-tower components and manufacturing inputs are executed by: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic-transfer wires for advance payments, deposits, and small-value balances; and (ii) irrevocable, confirmed, at-sight documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600, issued by the RMI-licensed bank and confirmed or negotiated by a top-tier U.S. or Asian bank for large shipments. For advance-payment protection, a standby Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT760) or an advance-payment bond may be issued in favor of the supplier. Each disbursement must be matched with the commercial invoice, packing list, transport document (airway bill or ocean bill of lading), certificate of origin, inspection certificate, and applicable Letter of Credit terms. The RMI imposes no restriction on the currency of payment, but USD-denominated settlement is recommended to eliminate FX conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards in USD/CNH, USD/EUR, and USD/JPY under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with prime international banks or licensed broker-dealers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to the onshore CNY (USD/CNY) fixing and other Asian restricted currencies where the onshore deliverable forward market is unavailable
Cross-currency swaps (CCS), including basis-swap structures, for hedging USD funding against EUR, GBP, or JPY receivables
Zero-cost collars and plain-vanilla FX options in USD/CNH and USD/EUR to protect minimum net margins on the endoscope-tower export contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Form AR) including registered agent details, director and officer particulars, share capital information, and payment of the annual franchise fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of US$250 where the report and fee are tendered after April 30; failure to file annual reports for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Registrar. Restoration after strike-off requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and applicable restoration fees.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a non-resident Business Corporation with no public securities listing, no banking or insurance licence, and no shareholder requisition. Under the Business Corporations Act, the Registrar may order an audit in exceptional cases, and holders of at least 5% of the relevant securities may compel an audit through court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed statutory GAAP is imposed by the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; books and records must reflect the corporation's financial condition accurately. IFRS or US GAAP is customarily applied where an audit or reviewed financial statement is voluntarily prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands registered agent is required under RMI AML/CFT law to maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register. There is no public annual UBO filing to the Registrar; however, the registered agent must receive an annual attestation from the corporate officer confirming the current beneficial owners. Any share transfer, beneficial ownership change, or increase in ownership must be notified to the registered agent generally within 14 days after the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 to US$1,500 per annum for a standard registered agent service, including registered office, annual report preparation, and filing handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000 to US$20,000 per annum for a voluntarily prepared independent audited financial statement; no mandatory audit fee is applicable to a low-transaction non-resident Business Corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporations with no Marshall Islands-source income, no local payroll, or no in-country fixed place of business are fully exempt from the Marshall Islands income tax and Business Revenue Tax (BRT). Foreign-source manufacturing and sales proceeds of medical devices are not subject to taxation. No capital duties, no VAT, and no annual franchise tax other than nominal registry filing fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry Online System – Annual Corporation Report (Form 6 – Corporate Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act 1990, s.109), filed electronically via www.micreregistrar.com.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 30 September of each calendar year for all active corporations; unless extended to the following business day when the 30th falls on a weekend or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the corporation, including any registered trade names.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name shown on the certificate of incorporation. This must match the corporate name used in all export transactions for the laparoscopy tower business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and registered office address in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a licensed registered agent resident in the Marshall Islands. The agent will be the primary contact for tax notices; no physical business presence is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of directors and principal officers, including names, addresses, and nationalities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may serve as directors; a non-resident entity may use professional or nominee directors. Beneficial ownership details must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML/CFT compliance but not filed publicly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total authorized and issued share capital, classes of shares, and par value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report capital in USD; no minimum capital requirement. No stamp duty or capital duty is levied on the share capital of the exempt non-resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity under the ISIC classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert 'ISIC 3250 – Manufacture of surgical and medical instruments; production of ultra-high-definition 4K minimally invasive rigid endoscopes and laparoscopic towers.' This confirms the manufacturing character for any tax authority audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemption declaration: confirm the corporation is non-resident and has no Marshall Islands-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick 'NON-RESIDENT EXEMPT' and certify that no business is conducted inside the Marshall Islands, no local payroll exists, and no permanent establishment is maintained. This declaration preserves the zero-rate tax status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a USD 100 penalty for the first month and USD 250 per month thereafter. Continued non-filing for more than one year triggers administrative dissolution by the Registrar. Reinstatement requires payment of all outstanding fees plus a USD 300 reinstatement charge. Directors of a dissolved entity may be held personally liable for obligations contracted during unauthorized trading.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands does not impose withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders. For inbound foreign-tax-credit purposes, a non-resident parent company may request a Certificate of Tax Status from the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance and Treasury; the certificate is submitted to the foreign tax authority to evidence that dividends have not suffered M.I. tax and, where a Double Tax Agreement exists (rare for M.I.), the relevant DTA residency article and Form 112/NRA materials apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% – the Marshall Islands does not tax gross royalties, license fees, or interest paid by a non-resident business corporation to foreign recipients. No withholding tax is charged on outbound interest or royalty flows, and no withholding formalities are prescribed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No domestic transfer-pricing (TP) legislation imposes local-file or master-file thresholds in the Marshall Islands. For a non-resident manufacturing SPV, arm's-length documentation is nevertheless recommended when intercompany cross-border transactions exceed USD 500,000 annually, to support the absence of M.I. taxable presence and to prevent recharacterization by home-country tax authorities.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands applies OECD-aligned Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to entities conducting 'relevant activities' (distribution, services, financing, holding, shipping, and intellectual property). Manufacturing of surgical endoscopes is not a listed relevant activity; therefore the non-resident BC is not subject to an economic substance test. It must, however, maintain a registered agent and file the annual corporate report; the directors must be able to demonstrate that central management control is exercised outside the Marshall Islands to avoid any argument of domestic tax residence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misuse of Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely declaring the entity to be non-resident while managing day-to-day manufacturing and contractual arrangements from the Marshall Islands, or using the M.I. shell to hide the substantive ownership of a profitable medical-device business from the home-country revenue authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Marshall Islands Income Tax Act 1989 and Business Corporations Act 1990, knowingly filing a false exemption declaration is a crime punishable by a fine of up to USD 25,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. The Ministry of Finance may also retroactively recharacterize the entity as resident and impose business revenue tax at the rate of 3% of gross revenue, with interest at 2% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are personally liable for the unpaid taxes and penalties up to the full outstanding amount. The Registrar can issue a travel ban and refer the case to the Attorney General for criminal forfeiture proceedings; equivalent foreign tax evasion may trigger extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the entity purely as a nominee-owned shell with no employees, no physical office, no real management decisions, and no independent bank accounts, while the surgical laparoscopy towers are actually produced and sold by related parties in onshore jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although manufacturing is outside the listed ESR relevant activities, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the Global Forum may require the registered agent to terminate the client relationship where the shell is used to facilitate tax crimes. Local law permits the Registrar to strike the company off the register; a 'serious default' declaration can result in a penalty of USD 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director knowingly allowing the company to be used as a sham vehicle is jointly and severally liable for foreign tax assessments; civil restitution orders and asset-freezing injunctions can be issued by the High Court of the Marshall Islands. The same director may be entered on the country's travel sanctions list pending cooperation with an international tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving wire transfers for the sale of laparoscopy towers through the M.I. bank account without filing a currency transaction report, or failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner when opening a transactions account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2022, financial and non-financial institutions must report suspected money laundering. Individual companies that fail to comply face civil penalties of up to USD 1,000,000; directors and officers may be subject to criminal fines of up to USD 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are personally liable for failing to implement know-your-customer (KYC) and beneficial-ownership controls. The Financial Intelligence Unit can issue a travel ban, freeze personal marital property, and prohibit the individual from leaving the country without permission. In egregious cases, extradition or prosecution abroad can follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Fraud / Profit Repatriation Sham
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing related-party royalty and licensing fees at inflated rates from a technology-owning M.I. subsidiary to an operating manufacturing affiliate, creating an artificial profit drain that reduces taxable income in the manufacturing jurisdiction and has no commercial economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Marshall Islands has no domestic TP statute, but the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework's Multilateral Institution may require the M.I. jurisdiction to cooperate in a cross-border tax audit. Under foreign tax law, the sham royalty arrangement can be recharacterized, resulting in a denial of deductions and penalty of 50% of the adjusted income. Local officers may additionally face perjury charges for falsely declaring the entity exempt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors who sign off on fraudulent intercompany agreements may incur personal liability for the foreign tax deficiency; leading courts have pierced the corporate veil to impose travel bans and disgorgement of personal bonuses. Under the Prevention of Fraud (M.I.) Act, any officer convicted of fraud is disqualified from serving as a director of any M.I. company for 10 years.
